state.misconception_label: Thinks alternate angles are always equal

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text:
I have: Tom and Katie are arguing about alternate angles. Tom says angles \( p \) and \( q \) are alternate. Katie says angles \( p \) and \( q \) are equal. Who is correct? ![Shows two non parallel lines that are intersected by another line. Angles P and Q are both on the outside of the lines and on opposite sides of the transversal.](). I got Only
Katie because I assumed all the angles in the figure are equal.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Alternate angles are not always equal. In the diagram you provided, angles \( p \) and \( q \) are alternate angles, but they are not necessarily equal. Alternate angles are only equal when the lines intersected by the transversal are parallel. Remember, in this case, the lines are not parallel.

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: Oh, I see! So angles \( p \) and \( q \) are only equal if the lines are parallel. But how do I know if the lines are parallel just by looking at a diagram? Can you explain that a bit more?

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: To determine if the lines are parallel, look for a pair of corresponding angles that are equal. If you can find a pair of corresponding angles that are equal, then the lines are parallel. Keep in mind that if the lines are not parallel, alternate angles will not be equal.

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: Okay, I think I get it a bit more now! So if I see two angles that are equal and they’re in the same position on different lines, then those lines must be parallel. But what if I can’t find any corresponding angles? How can I tell if the lines are parallel then?

score.justification_pass1: The teacher directly addresses the misconception with accurate content and the student shows clear improvement in understanding the parallel-lines condition, but the teacher simply tells rather than eliciting reasoning, and scaffolding could better match the student's demonstrated understanding level.
score.justification_pass2: The teacher consistently states explicit rules about alternate angles and parallel lines, provides direct corrective feedback on the student's misconception, and explains clear procedures for identifying parallel lines, which aligns well with the rule-based strategy.
